gloss: the war dead; those who died in war

definitions.gloss: the war dead; those who died in war
definitions.explanation: People who lost their lives in a war, typically referring to soldiers killed in battle but sometimes extended to all war casualties. Used in formal and commemorative contexts.

examples.japanese: {戦没者|せんぼつしゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{追悼|ついとう}→追悼：14312_tsuitou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧⟦{八月|はちがつ}→八月：00626_hachigatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{戦没者|せんぼつしゃ}⟦{追悼式|ついとうしき}→追悼式：24788_tsuitoushiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{行|おこな}われる→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: A memorial ceremony for the war dead is held every August.

examples.japanese: ⟦{首相|しゅしょう}→首相：03217_shushou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{戦没者|せんぼつしゃ}{墓苑|ぼえん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れ→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧、⟦{花束|はなたば}→花束：03135_hanataba⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捧|ささ}げた→捧げる：02055_sasageru⟧。
examples.english: The Prime Minister visited the cemetery for the war dead and laid a bouquet of flowers.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{戦|せん}→〜戦：28346_sen⟧ (war, battle), {没|ぼつ} (to pass away, literally "to sink"), and the suffix ⟦{者|しゃ}→〜者：04662_sha⟧ (person). The kanji {没|ぼつ} is used in formal contexts for death, especially in obituaries and memorial inscriptions. {戦没者|せんぼつしゃ} is a solemn, formal word found in news coverage, government statements, and the names of monuments and ceremonies — it is not used in casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {戦没者|せんぼつしゃ}⟦{追悼式|ついとうしき}→追悼式：24788_tsuitoushiki⟧: memorial ceremony for the war dead
- {戦没者|せんぼつしゃ}{墓苑|ぼえん}: cemetery for the war dead
- {戦没者|せんぼつしゃ}⟦{慰霊|いれい}→慰霊：22918_irei⟧: consolation of the spirits of the war dead
- {戦没者|せんぼつしゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{悼|いた}む→悼む：12622_itamu⟧: to mourn the war dead

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {戦死者|せんししゃ}: those killed in battle — more specifically, those who died fighting
- ⟦{犠牲者|ぎせいしゃ}→犠牲者：18769_giseisha⟧: victim — broader; can refer to any cause of death or harm
- {英霊|えいれい}: heroic spirits of the war dead — emotionally charged, honorific term
